body:
The Philadelphia Flyers and [NexGen Hyperbaric](https://nexgenhyperbaric.com/) today announced a multi-year extension of their partnership, continuing a relationship that has integrated true medical-grade hyperbaric oxygen therapy into the organization's comprehensive approach to player health, recovery and performance. 

The extension carries the partnership into the 2026-27 NHL season and beyond, building upon multiple seasons of direct experience between NexGen and the Flyers' physicians, medical professionals, athletic trainers and performance staff. 

Through NexGen's [patented mobile hyperbaric platform,](https://nexgenhyperbaric.com/enhancing-play-performance-recovery/) the Flyers have direct access to medical-grade hyperbaric oxygen therapy within the team's existing sports medicine environment. The platform was developed to bring the clinical capabilities, equipment and safety standards associated with hospital-based hyperbaric medicine directly to professional sports organizations without compromising the medical-grade standard. 

NexGen's professional sports platform delivers 100% oxygen at therapeutic hyperbaric pressures using FDA-cleared, U.S.-manufactured medical-grade monoplace hyperbaric chambers engineered to applicable ASME PVHO-1 and NFPA 99 standards. 

For the Flyers, the extension represents more than continued access to another recovery modality. It reflects multiple seasons of firsthand experience with NexGen's technology, clinical personnel and approach to medical-grade hyperbaric oxygen therapy. 

The extension also comes as the Flyers continue to advance an integrated approach to athlete performance and wellness under Daniel Bove, Vice President, Athlete Performance & Wellness. 

Bove joined the Flyers in 2026 following approximately a decade in the NBA, most recently serving as Vice President of High Performance for the New Orleans Pelicans. His career also includes performance and sports science roles with the Phoenix Suns and Atlanta Hawks. 

"At the professional level, there has to be a high standard for the technologies and modalities we put around our athletes," said Bove. "Medicine, performance, recovery and rehabilitation can't operate independently. They have to work together as part of a comprehensive approach to the athlete. That's why understanding the distinction between medical-grade hyperbaric oxygen therapy and other forms of hyperbaric exposure matters. With NexGen, we're talking about FDA-cleared medical equipment, 100% oxygen delivered at therapeutic hyperbaric pressure, established pressure-vessel and fire-safety standards, clinical protocols and integration with our medical and performance teams. 

Being able to bring that level of infrastructure directly into a professional sports environment gives our staff another resource as we continue to focus on player health, recovery, availability and performance throughout the demands of an NHL season." 

The renewed agreement further strengthens a relationship the Flyers say has continued to develop through direct experience and a shared commitment to player health. 

**TRUE MEDICAL-GRADE HYPERBARIC OXYGEN THERAPY: THE DISTINCTION MATTERS** 

As hyperbaric technologies have become increasingly visible throughout professional sports, recovery and wellness, understanding the distinction between medical-grade hyperbaric oxygen therapy and other forms of hyperbaric exposure has become increasingly important. 

Not everything marketed as "hyperbaric" is equivalent to medical-grade hyperbaric oxygen therapy. 

NexGen's professional sports platform delivers 100% oxygen at therapeutic hyperbaric pressures using FDA-cleared medical-grade equipment within a clinically managed environment. 

This differs materially from many lower-pressure "mild hyperbaric" systems marketed for athletic recovery and wellness. Many such systems pressurize the chamber primarily with ambient air, while some supplement oxygen through an oxygen concentrator. 

An oxygen concentrator does not, by itself, transform a mild hyperbaric exposure into medical-grade hyperbaric oxygen therapy. 

The differences extend beyond oxygen concentration. Operating pressure, chamber construction, medical-device status, oxygen delivery, pressure-vessel engineering, fire-safety requirements, clinical protocols, trained personnel and medical oversight all contribute to the distinction between a medical hyperbaric program and other forms of hyperbaric exposure. For professional sports organizations entrusted with the health and careers of elite athletes, those distinctions matter. 

**MAKING THE MEDICAL STANDARD MOBILE** 

NexGen's patented mobile hyperbaric platform was developed around a straightforward premise: making hyperbaric medicine mobile should never require lowering the medical standard. 

Rather than adapting lower-pressure wellness technology for professional athletes, NexGen brings true medical-grade hyperbaric oxygen therapy directly into the team's environment. The platform integrates medical-grade chambers, 100% oxygen delivery, safety systems, clinical protocols and experienced personnel into a mobile solution designed to operate alongside an organization's existing physicians, athletic trainers and performance professionals. The result is not a separate "sports version" of hyperbaric medicine. It is medical-grade hyperbaric oxygen therapy delivered within the professional sports environment. 

That distinction is rooted in NexGen's broader clinical foundation. NexGen operates nationally across three primary areas: hospital-based hyperbaric and wound care programs, freestanding hyperbaric treatment facilities, and professional sports medicine. Within professional sports, NexGen's platform has been integrated with organizations across the NFL, NHL and MLB, bringing the same commitment to medical-grade technology, clinical standards and safety that underpins the company's hospital-based and freestanding clinical operations directly into elite sports environments. 

For Jonathan Rotella, President and CEO of NexGen Hyperbaric, that continuum is central to both NexGen's identity and its relationship with the Flyers. 

"We are incredibly honored to extend our relationship with the Philadelphia Flyers," said Rotella. "What makes this partnership particularly meaningful is that it has been built through experience and trust. The Flyers' 

medical and athletic training professionals have worked alongside us and understand firsthand what true medical-grade hyperbaric oxygen therapy looks like and the value it can bring as part of a comprehensive approach to player health and recovery." 

"NexGen is a national hyperbaric medicine company. We develop and manage hospital-based programs, operate freestanding clinical facilities and have built a professional sports medicine division working across the NFL, NHL and MLB. We didn't build a wellness company and then add hyperbaric chambers. Hyperbaric medicine is our business, and the medical standard we apply in a hospital follows us into professional sports." 

"Our patented mobile platform allows us to bring that same standard directly to the team. We deliver 100% oxygen at therapeutic hyperbaric pressure using FDA-cleared medical-grade chambers manufactured in the United States and engineered to established ASME PVHO-1 and NFPA 99 standards. We don't lower the standard simply because we're operating in a professional sports environment." 

"There is a tremendous amount of confusion in the marketplace today. Mild hyperbaric chambers and systems supplemented with oxygen concentrators are increasingly marketed using terminology and claimed benefits associated with medical-grade hyperbaric oxygen therapy as though the technologies are interchangeable. They are not. Putting an oxygen concentrator next to a mild hyperbaric chamber does not make it medical-grade hyperbaric oxygen therapy." 

"Those aren't marketing distinctions. Pressure matters. Oxygen concentration matters. The medical device matters. Engineering and fire-safety standards matter. Clinical oversight matters. When you're talking about medicine and the health of professional athletes, those distinctions should matter." 

"The Flyers have understood and embraced that standard from the beginning. We are extremely proud to be associated with this organization and honored by the trust they continue to place in NexGen. We look forward to continuing to work alongside Alex, Daniel, Barry and the entire Flyers organization and playing a role in the health, recovery and success of its players for the years ahead." 

The extension continues a partnership built around a shared principle: when hyperbaric oxygen therapy is incorporated into an elite professional sports medicine environment, the quality of the technology, the oxygen being delivered, the clinical environment and the standards governing its delivery matter. 

**ABOUT NEXGEN HYPERBARIC** 

NexGen Hyperbaric is a national provider of medical-grade hyperbaric oxygen therapy programs serving hospitals, health systems, freestanding clinical facilities and professional sports organizations across the United States. 

The company operates across three principal areas: hospital-based hyperbaric and wound care programs, freestanding hyperbaric treatment facilities, and professional sports medicine. NexGen partners with hospitals and health systems to develop and manage comprehensive hyperbaric and wound care programs; operates freestanding clinical facilities providing access to medical-grade hyperbaric oxygen therapy; and, through its patented mobile hyperbaric platform, brings true medical-grade hyperbaric oxygen therapy directly to professional sports organizations. 

NexGen's professional sports division works with organizations across the NFL, NHL and MLB, integrating medical-grade hyperbaric oxygen therapy directly into existing team medical, athletic training, rehabilitation and performance infrastructures. 

NexGen's professional sports systems deliver 100% oxygen at therapeutic hyperbaric pressures using FDA-cleared medical-grade hyperbaric chambers manufactured in the United States and engineered to applicable ASME PVHO-1 and NFPA 99 standards. 

Across its hospital, clinical and professional sports operations, NexGen maintains the same core standard: medical-grade technology, 100% oxygen delivery, rigorous safety and engineering standards, experienced clinical personnel, and integration with the healthcare professionals responsible for patient and athlete care. 

From hospitals and freestanding clinical facilities to professional sports organizations, NexGen's mission remains consistent: to expand responsible access to true medical-grade hyperbaric oxygen therapy while maintaining the clinical standards that define the practice of hyperbaric medicine.
